title: Fight Club
synopsis: Insomnia, soap, a basement, and a man in the mirror who has finally caught up to you.

nodes.text: Cancer rooms full of hugs and a real grief that is not yours.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Cry honestly.” The story records the instinct as “Honest” and carries it forward.
You commit to “Fake it.” The story records the instinct as “Cold” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: She is a tourist too, and she sees you the way you see her.

choices.consequence: “Confront her” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Bold.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Cowardly—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Outside a bar, on a curb, his request.

nodes.text: You stand at a window with Marla's small fingers in yours and watch your debt erase itself in dust. Tomorrow has not been invented yet.
You go to a meeting and talk, finally, about the second man in your mirror. The room listens. The room has heard this before.
She takes you home. She asks your real name. You give it. It is the first thing you have said out loud in months that you actually meant.
